delta: Added tools/one-axis-physical-proof-gate.mjs to classify a One-Axis packet no higher than SPECIFIED, BUILT or TESTED from explicit physical evidence fields.
TESTED now requires ten unloaded and ten loaded measured runs, thermal observations, explicit anomalies, interruption recovery, return-to-zero, payload-adapter swap and evidence references.
The gate computes error summaries but does not invent pass tolerances; acceptance of physical quality remains attached to the referenced specification and observations.
ADOPTED is deliberately outside the gate: TESTED never implies repeated real-world adoption.
Added deterministic self-tests proving incomplete packets fail closed and a structurally complete synthetic packet reaches TESTED only.
value: Future workers can feed a physical receipt to one command instead of re-arguing proof state from prose.
Rich diagrams/BOMs can no longer satisfy the TESTED gate by themselves.
The gate preserves the physical-world boundary: software validates evidence structure, not whether a claimed measurement truly occurred.
The next useful work is a real measurement packet, not another hardware architecture document.
authority: Explicit user request on 2026-09-30 to turn the convergence loop into usable empirical machinery while keeping the reducer tight.
runtime_changes: One repository CLI validator plus CI self-test; no public route or actuator authority.
residue: No real One-Axis physical receipt exists yet.
No numeric accuracy tolerance is promoted by this gate; the historical spec versions differ and a real build must bind to an exact spec_ref.
PhoneCassette and rover paths remain outside this One-Axis-specific gate.
next: When physical work occurs, record the raw One-Axis observations and run: node tools/one-axis-physical-proof-gate.mjs <receipt.json>.
stop: Do not generalize this into a universal hardware ontology until a second distinct physical project proves the abstraction is needed.
summary: Cluster-14 convergence established SPECIFIED != BUILT != TESTED != ADOPTED, but the repository had no executable guard preventing a detailed hardware specification from being represented as TESTED without physical run evidence.
